title: Synthetic Security Controls
source: Original synthetic statements authored for Policy Evidence Agent tests

passages.text: Every workforce member must use an individually assigned account; shared user accounts are prohibited.
Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrator access.
System owners review user access at least quarterly and document the review.
Permissions are granted according to least privilege and job responsibilities.
Passwords are stored using an approved salted, one-way password hashing function.
The requester's identity must be verified before a password is reset.
Accounts and access tokens are disabled promptly when employment ends.
Service-account credentials are stored in an approved secrets manager and rotated regularly.
Sensitive data stored on managed systems is encrypted using organization-approved cryptography.
Sensitive data transmitted over untrusted networks uses current, approved transport encryption.
Encryption keys are restricted to authorized roles and kept separate from protected data.
Sensitive data on removable media must be encrypted and the media physically controlled.
Critical systems are backed up at least daily according to their recovery requirements.
A protected backup copy is isolated from routine production credentials and access.
Restoration tests are performed at least quarterly and their results are recorded.
Recovery copies are stored in a separate failure domain from the systems they protect.
Personnel must report suspected security incidents promptly through the designated incident channel.
The designated incident response lead coordinates investigation, containment, and recovery.
Incident records include the timeline, impact, decisions, and corrective actions.
After-action reviews identify lessons and track corrective actions to completion.
Systems record authentication, privileged activity, security configuration changes, and relevant access events.
Access to security logs is restricted, and log integrity is protected from unauthorized alteration.
Security logs are retained for at least one year unless a longer legal or contractual period applies.
Security monitoring alerts are reviewed for suspicious activity by authorized personnel.
A risk-based security review is completed before a new service provider receives company data or access.
Provider agreements document applicable confidentiality, security, incident notification, and data handling duties.
Important service providers are reassessed at least annually and after material changes.
At engagement end, the provider returns or securely deletes company data and confirms completion.
Employees complete security awareness training at least annually.
New employees receive security and acceptable-use training during onboarding.
Training completion and assigned follow-up are recorded in the learning system.
Employees are instructed to report suspicious messages through the designated reporting tool or channel.
Managed systems are scanned for vulnerabilities on a recurring schedule and after significant changes.
Security updates are prioritized by severity, exploitability, and business exposure.
High-risk vulnerabilities are mitigated within defined response targets or receive documented risk approval.
Remediation is verified by rescanning or equivalent evidence and tracked to closure.
Production changes require documented risk review and approval by an authorized owner.
Emergency changes are documented and receive retrospective review within the defined review period.
Changes are tested in a suitable non-production environment before release when feasible.
Production changes record the requester, approver, implementation time, and outcome.
